doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: Basie band: origins, sound and style
title: Why Basie was called Chief
summary: Foster and Hughes recall that the Chief nickname arose in the late 1950s, that they called him Bas, and the Superchief album.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: How did he get that nickname, “Chief?”
I don’t remember when that first came into play.
I think that started back either in the late 50’s or, yeah, it was the late 50’s.
Late 50’s, yeah, because early 50’s I’m pretty sure we weren’t calling him “Chief.”
None of us ever called him Count.
No. People would come up to him, you know, lay people would come and say “Hello Count.”
Wasn’t there an album, with a picture of a train, and him on the front?
“Superchief.” Well he was called Chief long before that album came out.
